answer: A planned controlled cutover is unsuitable when an essential source-side condition cannot be met: source writes cannot be paused, or replication completeness cannot be verified. In practice this means unresolved DLQ errors or permanent forward-replication errors prevent a clean pause, or data freshness cannot reach zero after the write pipeline drains. Because authority must not switch until source changes have fully replicated, these are hard contraindications: defer the cutover or use an alternative such as Strangler Fig, rolling/blue-green deployment, or a canary with a reversible gate.
